plate.viewWhy: As for the parent: long arms, a tall body and a straight-up shoulder path read best side-on (c1, c2); the census draws it side.
plate.equipment: Smith machine (rails, bar, hooks); bar at mid-thigh height in front of the body (c1); safety pins set (c4); floor line.
plate.start: Standing, feet shoulder-width (c1), arms hanging long with a slight elbow bend, bar at mid-thigh (c1), shoulders relaxed down (c2).
plate.end: Same body; only the shoulders lifted straight up toward the ears, arms still long (c2).

checkpoints.label: Arms long
checkpoints.what: Elbows keep only a slight bend; the arms just hang.

checkpoints.label: Straight up
checkpoints.what: Shoulders go up toward the ears and back down, no roll.

checkpoints.label: Head still
checkpoints.what: Head stays level, not pushed forward.

mistake.what: Elbows bending to pull the bar up instead of the shoulders lifting it.
mistake.why: Motra names excessive elbow bend among the common Smith shrug mistakes, and it reads side-on. Rolling the shoulders is a rotation the engine cannot draw. How often each happens is not measured.

grip.thumb: Wrapped around the bar (inherited, parent c10).
grip.handContact: Bar across the middle of the palm, fingers wrapped (inherited, hold archetype).
grip.wrist: Not given by any shrug source read (hold archetype default).

handlingMistakes.mistake: Rocking the body to swing the bar up.
handlingMistakes.fix: Use slow, steady reps; add weight only in small steps.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Bending the elbows to pull the bar.
handlingMistakes.fix: Keep the arms long; lift with the shoulders.
